newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK quality of life lower than rival cities - poll.
newsitem.headline: HK quality of life lower than rival cities - poll.

text.p: The quality of life in Hong Kong is lower than some Asian cities that are often seen as the British colony's main competitors, a survey showed on Friday.
In a poll on life quality conducted by Asiaweek magazine, Hong Kong scored 61 points out of 100, while Tokyo scored 71 and Singapore 67. Hong Kong ranked sixth among 40 Asian cities surveyed.
"When we talk about quality of life, Hong Kong has a lot going for it with good entertainment and social facilities and a low tax rate," Asiaweek editor Ann Morrison said.
Hong Kong people enjoyed a maximum tax rate of 15 percent, half that of Singapore and less than a third of Tokyo, she said.
"However, we cannot get away from the fact that Hong Kong is a very expensive place to live with the cost of housing being a very significant factor," she said.
Hong Kong was eighth highest in the cost of buying a home at US$8,250 per square metre, compared with US$5,117 in Singapore. But Tokyo is even more expensive, at $8,500 per square metre.
"We should not lose sight of the fact that Hong Kong is still up there with the best, although there is a significant gap with Singapore," Morrison said.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty next year after more than 150 years of British rule.
The criteria used for quality of life in the survey covered economic opportunity, schools, health care, roads and public transport, housing, crime, living environment and leisure.
